nodePolicies.description: Named exclusion policies applied to internal node path declarations. Exclusion values are ordinary path patterns; the engine negates them when expanding a policy. Default policies apply automatically; node object specs may add a policy by name or remove a default policy with !name.

nodes.description: All architecture nodes (vertices). Maps logical node IDs to internal path templates or external identifiers. For internal paths, prefix pattern with `!` to exclude files from the same node mapping. Node path patterns must not reference other node IDs (`@...`); repeat globs explicitly or generate config. Engine warns when one node include pattern fully contains another node include pattern without explicit exclusion boundaries.

graph.description: Directed edge definition. Supports flat graph or named subgraphs.

rules.description: Policy overrides for graph edge checks. Used for temporary debt waivers or local policy gates.

oneOf.description: Single path template (supports [var], *, **, ?) or external key like npm:react / node:fs.

policies.description: Exact named policy references. name adds a policy; !name removes a default policy.

default.description: Apply this policy to every node containing internal path patterns unless the node removes it with !name.

items.description: A non-negated path pattern. The engine adds the exclusion marker when expanding the policy.

targetNode.description: Node selector. Use exact id for strict match, or explicit glob for wildcard match (e.g. @core:**).

edgePolicySeverity.description: Outcome when the rule matches (rules are evaluated in array order; first match wins). `error`: always forbid the edge. `warn`: allow with warning. `off`: allow and silence. Omitting the field defaults to `error`.

ruleScope.description: `all`: always run matchers (default). `fallback`: only when the abstract graph denies the edge (debt exemption / illegal-edge patch). `topology_allowed`: only when the graph allows the edge (e.g. deprecation on legally allowed dependencies without downgrading illegal edges).

ruleMatcher.description: Pattern list for one side. `!` at string start means negation. @-prefixed values match logical nodes, others match physical paths/import specs. If all patterns are negated, matcher uses implicit universe and then subtracts negations. Placeholders `[name]` (alphanumeric/underscore) are template variables: on `from` they are extracted from the node or path, then substituted into `to` patterns in the same rule (cross-edge unification). If every `from` pattern is negated, none of them may contain `[name]` (a complement is not a finite set to extract from). Patterns without `[name]` still use glob matching.
